findings.reason: §16's own done-when requires the census to report one expression, and as written no reviewer can satisfy it for this site; the plan must exempt the word-binder or specify a shared number core rather than the whole anchored expression.
findings.text: §16 requires every section-spelling grammar site to converge on one shared expression and names `roadmap._SECTION_WORD_RE` among them, but `_SECTION_WORD_RE` (`\b(?:section|sections)\s+(\d+(?:...)*)`) binds a *list* of numbers anywhere in gate prose ("sections 5 and 6") while the shared expression `_SECTION_IDENTITY` (`reckon/crew/routing.py:219`) is an anchored single-identity full-match; the two are not the same grammar, so the mandated convergence is unachievable without moving the anchors, which §16 does not authorize

findings.reason: the reader can call one shared classification predicate and still preserve document order, so either extract that predicate for doccheck to call or drop the "one place" claim; leaving it makes the §18 done-when's one-place assertion false.
findings.text: §18 states the landing rule "changes in one place" and expresses `_schema.plan_executable_remainder` over `roadmap.implementable_sections`, yet leaves `doccheck._implementable_section_ids` comparing each declaration against the literal `"implementable"` inline, the same classification predicate as `implementable_sections` (`reckon/roadmap.py:106`); document order and the heading-id fallback are a different output, not a different rule, so the rule is spelled in two places after §18

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §17 consolidates section enumeration, identity and extent behind one private parser and one public `plan_headings` reader with named fields, replacing several ad-hoc walks; §16's `_section_digests` and coverage predicate are module-private and the public `plan_fingerprint` signature does not widen (the `legacy` flag is retired).
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §16 mandates that roadmap's `_SECTION_WORD_RE` converge on the shared section-identity expression, and §18 leaves `doccheck._implementable_section_ids` re-implementing the "still implementation work" classification rule instead of extending `roadmap.implementable_sections`.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1477, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §17 names in its own text its two added public definitions (`plan_headings`, the machinery-element predicate) and the private walks it retires (net +2), and §16 and §18 each state no public definition is added or retired and reuse the existing plan-review-missing refusal family, so no family grows without account.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan searched and extends existing machinery rather than adding a parallel subsystem: `_StructuredSectionSpanParser`/`structured_section_spans` (`reckon/_plan_html.py:44,94`), `plan_fingerprint`/`_fingerprint_forms`/`_authored_prose`/`_AuthoredProseParser` (`reckon/crew/plan_review.py:162,257,368,598`), `roadmap.implementable_sections` (`reckon/roadmap.py:106`), `_schema.plan_executable_remainder` (`reckon/_schema.py:788`) and `promotion._landed_sections` (`reckon/roadmap` symbols all confirmed present at the named revisions); no existing per-section digest or public section reader was found, so §16's and §17's additions are new rather than duplicative.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §18's `plan_executable_remainder` is not a bare forward: it retains the missing/malformed-declaration unknown sentinel (`reckon/_schema.py:798-806`) and delegates only the classification comparison, and §16/§17 move recognisers and helpers to their owners rather than layering wrappers over them.
